comment: CDIF has no Study entity. A DISCO Study is the process that collected the data, which CDIF carries as the activity in prov:wasGeneratedBy; the Study's descriptive metadata (title, abstract, creator, funder) belongs on the CDIF Dataset. One Study therefore splits across two CDIF nodes.
No CDIF target. schema:hasPart carries four distinct meanings in CDIF and none of them is 'wave of a longitudinal series' - for review.

Both denote the logical dataset, but LogicalDataSet is rdfs:subClassOf dcat:Dataset while CDIF roots on schema:Dataset. Neither is a subclass of the other, so this is a translation boundary and NOT a co-typing: a node typed both ways asserts two unrelated classes.
rdfs:subClassOf dcat:Distribution; same base-class caveat as LogicalDataSet. Spelled disco:Datafile in the spec's EXAMPLE 19.
A column of a rectangular data file in both models.
The same DDI concept reached by two routes: DISCO derives from DDI-Codebook/Lifecycle, the cdi: namespace from DDI-CDI. Not a reuse of one term.

DISCO Representation is a subclass of the UNION of rdfs:Datatype, skos:ConceptScheme and skos:OrderedCollection, and is ONE node. CDIF has no cdi:ValueDomain class and splits it three ways: cdif:physicalDataType / cdif:recommendedDataType carry the datatype, while the enumerated domain is either a cdif:SubstantiveValueDomain (subject-matter values) or a cdif:SentinelValueDomain (missing-value codes), reached by cdi:takesSubstantiveValuesFrom / cdi:takesSentinelValuesFrom. A DISCO Representation mixing real categories with missing-value codes must be partitioned, and nothing in DISCO says which code is which (see disco:isValid).
No CDIF target: no term for a target population exists in any of the 78 building blocks (measured 2026-11-24) - for review.

No CDIF target. schema:instrument in cdifProvenance is a physical measuring device (an XAS monochromator, say), not a data-collection instrument; equating the two would be wrong.

DISCO's abstract superclass of Summary- and CategoryStatistics. CDIF's collection is concrete and groups cdi:Statistics nodes.

DISCO carries each statistic in its own named property (mean, median, ...); CDIF carries cdif:typeOfStatistic plus a cdi:statistic array, so one DISCO SummaryStatistics node becomes SEVERAL CDIF Statistics nodes.

Study -> its datasets, inverted in CDIF: the Dataset is the root and names its generating activity, so the forward CDIF direction is prov:wasGeneratedBy. The range given in the spec's Vocabulary Reference, cube#LogicalDataSet, is a namespace error - the class is disco:LogicalDataSet.
Declared on both Study and LogicalDataSet. CDIF hangs variables off the Dataset only, so both rows land in the same place - this is why subject_class is needed.
No CDIF target; see disco:StudyGroup.
Only the enumerated branch maps here. A Representation that is an rdfs:Datatype goes to cdif:physicalDataType / cdif:recommendedDataType instead.
Also declared on disco:RepresentedVariable and disco:Question.
No CDIF target; see disco:Universe. Declared over six domains (Study, StudyGroup, RepresentedVariable, Variable, Question, LogicalDataSet).
No CDIF target; see disco:AnalysisUnit.
A skos:Concept in DISCO; schema:additionalType is CDIF's general classification slot and also carries profile and domain classification, so the mapping is lossy in the CDIF-to-DISCO direction.
No CDIF target; see disco:Instrument - schema:instrument denotes a different thing.
No CDIF target.
No CDIF target. Listed under Classes in spec section 11.2.1 (#10), which is an error - it is an object property.
No CDIF target.
Range foaf:Document. Maps only once the Instrument itself is dropped and its documentation is reattached to the Dataset.
Declared rdfs:subPropertyOf dcterms:contributor in DISCO. schema:funding carries the award where one is known.
DISCO relates a foaf:Agent to a skos:Concept role; CDIF uses a schema:Role wrapper carrying schema:roleName. Domain is not a DISCO class.
No CDIF target: CDIF has no RDF Data Cube bridge. The portable part is DISCO's own PROV pattern (prov:wasDerivedFrom, spec section 10.7.1), which CDIF does carry at $.prov:wasDerivedFrom.
No CDIF target. Marked a feature at risk in the spec because its domain is not DISCO.
A link to the source DDI-XML file. CDIF carries it as a linkRole whose schema:linkRelationship names the relation.
No CDIF target: CDIF attaches statistics to the variable, not to a distribution.
Inverted: DISCO points a statistics node at its variable, CDIF points a variable at its statistics.
The category the statistic is computed for; a skos:Concept in DISCO, a cdi:Category in CDIF.
Also declared on disco:CategoryStatistics.

A skos:Concept in both. NOTE the spec spells this summaryStatisticType in section 7.3 and summaryStatisticsType in the Vocabulary Reference appendix; both forms appear in the document and only one can be the real IRI.

xsd:boolean in DISCO. CDIF has no boolean here, so the flag becomes a conditionsOfAccess statement, or an odrl:Offer under the cdifAccess profile. Not reversible: a conditionsOfAccess string does not reduce to true/false.

DISCO puts these on a dcterms:PeriodOfTime inside dcterms:temporal; CDIF uses time:hasBeginning / time:inTimePosition inside schema:temporalCoverage (cdifDiscovery).
As disco:startDate, via time:hasEnd.
No CDIF target. Spelled disco:QuestionText in the spec's EXAMPLE 26 for two of three questions.

No CDIF target for a per-category validity flag; CDIF separates substantive from sentinel values structurally (cdi:takesSubstantiveValuesFrom / cdi:takesSentinelValuesFrom). Marked a feature at risk in the spec because its domain is not DISCO.
schema:description is one string with many sources; appending is the only safe treatment.
rdf:langString in DISCO, a closed enum (MissingOnly | Total | ValidOnly) in CDIF, so an arbitrary DISCO string will not validate.
